text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Around 28 percent of Poles support the ex-communist co-ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), 25 percent are ready to vote for the rightist Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) and 11 percent support the centrist Union for Freedom (UW), a June survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- The AWS and UW will support Wladyslaw Bartoszewski and Krzysztof Piesiewicz to run for the Senate in the September parliamentary elections.

- The Katowice provincial court in southern Poland has registered the so-called Silesian Nationals Association, a political wing of a controversial movement favouring the region's autonomy. The province's governor will appeal against the ruling at the court of appeals.

- Poland has reconstructed a rapidly developing market economy and joined the democratic countries of Europe, Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said at a meeting of the Council of Europe in Strasbourg on Wednesday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's budget deficit will have to be less than two percent in 1998, the Finance Minister Marek Belka said.

- The listed Stalexport steel maker and trader and the Huta Katowice steel mill have applied to Thailand's trade ministry to present full documentation on the recently passed anti-dumping duty regulations on Polish steel products, as the companies want to challenge the laws at the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

- Poland's finance ministry has cut the excise tax on fuels containing alcohol by 10 zlotys per tonne. The cut will benefit refineries located in southern Poland and distributor CPN, which produce the fuels.

- Poland's industrial development agency (ARP) reported its best results in 1996 since it was formed in 1991, agency president Arkadiusz Krezel said. Revenues grew by 62 percent, gross profit by 82 percent and the net profit by 18 percent compared with the year before. ARP's assets increased to 775 million zlotys from 621.9 million zlotys.
- France's Thomson Multimedia will invest 170 million French francs in the construction of a television assembly plant in Zyrardow, central Poland.

- The government's special economic committee (KERM) has decided to guarantee the EFSAL fund development credit of 5.1 million zlotys to go to the Madrat carpentry plant in Lublin, eastern Poland and 9.8-million-zloty credit for the Dozamet Metallurgical plant in Nowa Sol, western Poland.
- Poland's insurance firms invested 6.4 million zlotys in 1996, representing 10 percent of the country's bank deposits accumulated in the period, the state insurance supervision office (PUNU) said.
- Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) presented a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) on Wednesday, KPW said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The Pekao SA group will have to sell its stake in the Amplico Life insurer if it plans to take part in the privatisation of the PZU insurance firm, a source who declined to be named said.
- The market share of pirate software products in Poland has declined to 71 percent from 77 percent since 1994, the Business Software Alliance representative Ewa Podgorska said.
- The Fameg furniture maker plans to issue one million shares nominally worth 2.33 zlotys per share, Fameg board member Roman Swiercz said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Pekao SA group made a pre-tax profit of 882.1 million and net profit of 514 million zlotys.
ZYCIE
- Highly qualified salesman and unskilled workers stand a similar chance to find a job in Poland, a survey by the Gdansk market economy research institute said.
